title: Implement Queue using Stacks
hints: a stack gives you last-in-first-out access, but you need first-in-first-out - how could two stacks combined reverse order back to the order you need?
what if all pushes go into one stack, and pops/peeks come from a second stack that holds elements in reverse order?
when the second (output) stack is empty and you need to pop or peek, dump the entire first (input) stack into it - that reverses it into the correct front-to-back order
as long as you only refill the output stack when it's empty, each element only ever gets moved twice total, so operations are O(1) amortized
commonMistakes: popping from the input stack directly for a queue pop, which gives the most recently pushed element instead of the oldest
transferring elements between stacks on every single operation instead of only when the output stack is empty, losing the amortized efficiency
forgetting that empty must check both the input and output stacks, not just one
not preserving relative order when transferring between stacks (must pop-and-push one at a time so the order reverses)

content.problemStatement:
You need to implement a first-in-first-out (FIFO) queue, but the only
building block available to you internally is a stack, which is
last-in-first-out. You're given a space-delimited sequence of operations
to run against this queue, starting from an empty queue. Each token is
one of:

- `"push_<value>"` - add value to the back of the queue
- `"pop"` - remove and report the value at the front
- `"peek"` - report the value at the front without removing it
- `"empty"` - report 1 if the queue is currently empty, 0 otherwise

**Simulate the operations in order, and return a list containing the result of every "pop", "peek", and "empty" operation, in the order they occurred.**

You can assume "pop" and "peek" are never called on an empty queue.
constraints: tokens are separated by single spaces, and push tokens join the operation and value with an underscore
push values fit in a standard 32-bit integer and may be negative
pop and peek are never called while the queue is empty
notes: empty called on a queue that has never had anything pushed
interleaved pushes and pops, not just push-then-pop-everything
a push happening between two pops of earlier-pushed elements
many pushes in a row before any pop or peek

sampleTestCases.explanation: queue holds [1,2] front-to-back; peek reports 1; pop removes and reports 1, leaving [2]; empty reports 0 since [2] remains
pop removes and reports the only element, 5; empty then reports 1 since the queue is now empty

sampleTestCases.input: ops = "push_3 push_4 pop push_5 peek pop pop empty"
sampleTestCases.explanation: FIFO order is preserved even though push_5 happens after the first pop: pop->3, peek/pop see 4 then 5, then the queue is empty

optimal.pattern: two stacks: an input stack for pushes, an output stack for pop/peek, refilled lazily

bruteForce.approach: for every pop or peek, reverse the entire input stack into a temporary stack to reach the bottom (oldest) element, use it, then reverse everything back
